doc.title: John Best interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Parents and a leader who kept the money
summary: His mother wanted him to be a preacher; a college-circuit leader pocketed the band's pay.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your parents, were they supportive of your interest in music as you grew up? Or did they want you to be something else?

My mother wanted me to be a preacher. I think my dad — whatever I did I was his favorite. But the way it turned out, it just kept working. I never studied music you know. I always regretted that. But I liked to play and I just liked songs, you know, and it kept going. We never made any money. If we did make it, the leader would go off with it in those days. I remember we did a whole bunch of college stuff, Christmas holidays, in North Carolina and Virginia. And this guy took all the money. The next time we saw him he’s smoking an expensive cigar and has a beautiful suit of clothes.
